instagram.author: drcolleenreichmann
instagram.body:
Had myself some fun trying to do these re-enactments of how I often react in sessions🤪

Sometimes I wish I could go back and show myself as a psychologist now to my grad school self-the one who was so concerned with not crossing her legs and keeping her face neutral. 

In all seriousness, I think that the “blank slate” emphasis totally overlooks the fact that sometimes, your face and body language ARE the intervention. I really deeply believe that, alongside of evidenced based tools, there is healing that happens for when you *truly* listen and react with your full expression. 

And one last piece on this that I’ve been sitting with lately: expression-less listening was a technique that was developed long before the era of social media and smart phones-Prior to the epidemic of  everyone half-listening to each other in day to day conversations while also scrolling. Reflective, full body listening feels less and less common, so bringing it into the therapy space feels more important and clinically relevant today than ever before🤔

Looking for more support navigating your mental health?
Wildflower Therapy can help if you reside in PA, DE, FL, VA, VT, MA, NJ, OH, or SC. We offer virtual therapy and also offer in person therapy in center city Philadelphia or Devon, and have therapists who specialize in eating disorders, anxiety, OCD, depression, infertility, perinatal mental health, maternal mental health, and more.

Visit www.wildflowertherapyllc.com to fill out our referral form and request a free 30 minute consult with one of our therapists. Or just email wildflowertherapyllc@gmail.com
Our faces are a map of the world.

When you pay for Kaiser healthcare, you should be able to see a therapist, not consult an app. Support Kaiser therapists; don’t let Kaiser shortchange your care.
Hi, I'm Molly Parsons, a mental health therapist for Kaiser Permanente in Northern California. We all know that Kaiser has struggled to provide accessible mental healthcare. But as therapists, we were making Kaiser do better until now. With negotiations underway on our union contract, Kaiser is proposing to reverse the improvements we've won for Kaiser patients, eliminate our input into how we provide care for our patients, and reserve the right to lay off Kaiser therapists so it can outsource mental healthcare. This is happening as Kaiser is employing fewer therapists and investing millions in AI. How would you feel about a robot addressing your mental health concerns? I wouldn't be okay with that. Learn more about our fight and share your Kaiser mental health story at kaiser-dontdeny.org.

instagram.author: frictiontherapist
instagram.body:
A new mom’s chat logs were just used against her in court… by the same employer that provided the app..

Jennifer Kamrass thought she was somewhere safe. She was nine months pregnant, just fired, and typing her fears into a therapy app her employer paid for. Two years later those words were read in court.

This story was investigated and published by Proof News journalist Annie Gilbertson on April 28, 2026.

Here are the questions we have to be asking right now.

Who is holding this information and what authority did they earn to hold it?

Who gave them permission to use your most vulnerable moments to train their next product? Talkspace’s CEO told investors they have compiled 8 billion words, 140 million messages, 6.2 million assessments. That data is currently building a therapy chatbot. Jennifer did not consent to that.

What happens to everything you shared when the company gets sold? Last month Universal Health Services acquired Talkspace for 835 million dollars. Jennifer’s words are now assets on a balance sheet.

And what actually protects you when something goes wrong? Under HIPAA psychotherapy notes carry special protection. Jennifer’s chat messages were classified as the treatment itself, integrated directly into her medical record. That classification made everything she typed fully discoverable. HIPAA protected Talkspace legally. It did not protect Jennifer.

In one of my prior reels, I raised these questions about Guide AI and Spring Health as hypotheticals. Jennifer Kamrass shows us we are already past hypothetical.

This is happening right now. And the ai apps being built today are collecting more data than Talkspace ever did.

Talkspace’s own privacy policy stated: “If you do not want us to share personal data or feel uncomfortable with the ways we use information in order to deliver our Services, please do not use the Services”…

This content is for educational purposes only and does not constitute legal or clinical advice. Source: @proof__news April 28, 2026. 

https://www.proofnews.org/womans-talkspace-therapy-app-sessions-exposed-in-court/

#frictiontherapist #aiintherapy #therapy #adventhealth #talkspace
Y'all, this is already happening. A new mom's therapy chat logs were just used against her in court by the same employer who paid for her therapy app. Her name is Jennifer Camaras. Avin health fired her 9 months pregnant and she kept on using Talkspace, the mental health benefit they provided, and started typing about her fears with money, work, and raising a family and in the months that followed her termination, she filed a pregnancy discrimination claim. Her employer's lawyers got a court order for every single message she had ever sent to Talkspace, every word that she typed to her therapist, and it was produced in court, used against her. Now, here's the part that will make your stomach drop. Under HIPAA, psychotherapy notes carry a special protection, but Jennifer's messages were classified as the treatment itself integrated directly into her chart notes and that made everything she typed fully discoverable. The more she opened up, the more there was to subpoena. And while Jennifer was typing, Talkspace's CEO was telling investors that they had compiled 140 million messages, currently training a therapy chatbot set to release later this year and then last month, Universal Health Services acquired Talkspace. So, Jennifer's words, her crisis moments and her fears about her families, all that data was transferred to another company without her permission. And in my last reel, I talked about what could happen when employers hold your mental health data. Check out the guide AI real right below. But Jennifer Camaras shows us we are already past the hypothetical. This data is already being used against us. So we have to ask these questions right now: Who is holding this information? Who gave them permission to use our pain to train their next product? What happens when everything you shared in these AI apps gets sold to the next company and who is actually protecting you when something goes wrong? Because Jennifer thought she knew the answers to these questions but she didn't.

instagram.author: markmanson
instagram.body:
AI becomes dangerous when it replaces thinking but powerful when it improves it.
So, it turns out that AI is surprisingly good for personal growth and mental health support, but you're probably not using it right. So, here are three ways that you should be using AI to grow that doesn't involve simply asking Chat GPT for advice. Number one is rehearsing hard conversations. You can actually practice a difficult conversation before you actually have them. So, what you do is you go to the AI, you give it context and information about the person that you want to have this conversation with, and then the AI can actually coach you how to work through that conversation. Number two is processing decisions that you've been going in circles on. Oftentimes, we don't have clarity on our own decisions because we can't properly weigh all the variables that we're dealing with. So, it can be helpful to have a conversation partner ask us specific questions about what is important to us, what do we care about, what do we want to emphasize, what are we optimizing for, to get clarity on what actually matters to us. And it turns out that AI is a fantastic way to do this. In fact, I built an entire AI coach that does nothing but this. It's called Purpose, and you can check it out at purpose.app. Number three is tracking patterns over time. We're all used to doing habit trackers and tracking our meals and tracking our fitness, but what if you could track all those things and get feedback on what you're doing well and what you're not doing well, like the way a coach would give you feedback? Turns out, you can do this right in most AI apps. So, try any of these three things out. They're very easy to do, and I think you'll be blown away by the effect that they'll have on your life.
